title: Factorized derived inverse mate normalization
statement: For finite R, p:X→Y, and a cochain complex P of fixed-scalar modules on Y, the expanded representative equation holds with the exact-derived inverse-image isomorphism and mapDerivedCategoryFactors displayed separately before replacing their composite by the left-derived counit. This is the strict intermediate used to prove the counit-form equation.

source.place: Tags 07A6 and 0D6E; factorized derived mate normalization

proof.text: Unfold finiteScalarOrdinaryPullbackComparison as the inverse mate of the ordinary normalized direct-image comparison. The forward mates equivalence recovers that direct-image comparison, including the equality identifying the two constant-coefficient pushforwards.

Localize the ordinary inverse-image square with mapDerivedCategorySquareIso. Apply the proved generic simple_derived_mate_factors helper from the fixed-scalar restriction/direct-image module. Its right-derived unit equation is the same as sfIntrinsicDerivedDirectImageComparison_inv_unitQ_factors after transporting the constant-pushforward equality. On K-injective complexes the source unit is invertible, so cancellation of that unit and of the target localization factor identifies the two right mates. Every derived object has a K-injective representative, and naturality along the representative isomorphism extends equality to all objects. Injectivity of the mates equivalence identifies the inverse-image squares.

Transport the exact-derived adjunction along leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory; the proved restriction_derived_adj_eq and mate_left_iso helpers give precisely finiteScalarPullbackComparison followed by the exactness isomorphism. The composition and natural-isomorphism factorization equations for mapDerivedCategorySquareIso compute its component on Q(P). Postcompose by the inverse ordinary complex comparison and cancel the two comparison components. Finally cancel finiteScalarPullbackComparison.hom on the left to obtain exactly the displayed factorized equation.

proof_origin.place: Tags 07A6 (lemma-adjoint) and 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition); exact localization, right-derived unit normalization, and uniqueness of mates.
